coordinator_note: Every theoretical value read against its quotes. Chia's results are HIGH where the statement and conditions are quoted and only a fraction's layout is lost (Corollary 6.4, Lemmas 3.13 and 4.3); LOW where a bound is garbled past reading (Corollary 6.5, Theorem 6.3, Lemma 4.5), where conditions or conclusion are not quoted, or where the proof is a sketch. Coroi's main theorems are quoted whole and stay HIGH. Coyle's Table 1 and overfitting figures come from a text layer that interleaves columns and panels, so they stay LOW

qsl-cor-6-4-distinguishing: Corollary 6.4 is stated with all conditions in Section 6.2 and proved from Theorem 6.3.
qsl-def-learnable-distinguishable: Section 4 defines the learning and distinguishing notions the main results depend on.
qsl-lemma-4-3-robustness: Stated with conditions and proved from Fact 2.3 and Corollary 2.6.
qsl-def-prs: Section 3 defines the pseudorandom object the lower-bound argument uses.
qsl-lemma-3-13-state-vs-decision: Stated with conditions and proved in Section 3.2.
qsl-lemma-2-17-circuit-count: Stated with its condition and proved in Section 2.3.2.
qsl-cor-2-6-multicopy: Stated and proved from Fact 2.5 in Section 2.1.1.
qsl-scope-circuit-class-restrictions: Section 1 and Section 2.3.2 state the conditions on the circuit class.
qsl-remark-nonuniformity: Remark 2.16 and Section 5 state this as a difference in definitions that limits direct transfer.
qsl-limit-no-adaptive-pru: Sections 1.1.4 and B.2 state these limits and open problems.
qsl-limit-prs-roadblock: Section 1.3 states the roadblock and open direction.
qsl-trivial-learners-appendix-d: Appendix D states which parameter regimes are trivial, and so what the nontrivial threshold is.
qsl-remark-fine-grained-size: Remark 6.6 states the scope of the learner assumed.
coelho-nystrom-definition: Section 4 defines the method the results depend on.
coelho-kta-definition: Section 3 defines the kernel and cost used throughout; the KTA cost follows Hubregtsen et al.
coelho-datasets: The Appendix specifies the benchmark data.
coelho-hyperparameter-limit: Section 6.1 states these limits of the evidence.
coelho-depolarizing-model: Section 6.3 states the noise model and its limit.
coroi-bm-protocol: Theorem 1 is stated with its resource conditions in the main text and proved in the Supplemental Material (Theorem S6 and Corollary S7) with Hoeffding's inequality and a union bound.
coroi-ef-lower-bound: Theorems 2 and 3 are stated with their conditions in the main text and proved in full in the Supplemental Material (Sections S6 and S7) by a revealed hypothesis-testing reduction and a total variation distance bound.
coroi-def-learning-task: Definition 1 and Definition S1 define the task all bounds refer to.
coroi-def-reflected-state: The main text defines the resource on which the protocol depends.
coroi-corollary-s7-post-measurement-quer: Corollary S7 is stated with its conditions and proved by a two-case argument.
coroi-three-peak-family-scope: The main text states the family on which the bounds are proved and why that suffices.
coroi-theorem-4-no-reflected-state: Theorem 4 is stated with its conditions in the main text and proved in Section S8.
coroi-upper-bound-heterodyne: The heterodyne estimator and its Hoeffding bound are derived in Section S9.
coroi-lemma-s5-tail-bound: Lemma S5 is stated with its condition and proved in two lines.
coroi-theorem-6-classicality-lower: Theorem 6 is stated with its admissibility conditions and proved as Theorem S15; the Supplement states where the bound becomes trivial.
coroi-classicality-tradeoff-claim: The main text states the open case explicitly.
coyle-density-qnn-mixing-lemma: Lemma 1 is stated with its assumptions in the Results and proved in Supplementary B.2 from the Hastings-Campbell mixing lemma.
coyle-def-density-qnn: Results p.2 defines the model family on which all results are stated.
coyle-def-backprop-scaling: Definition 1 states the efficiency notion used for the trainability claims (the definition is taken from earlier work).
coyle-equivariant-setup: The Methods state the experimental configuration.
coyle-equivariant-simulability-limit: Stated by the authors in the Results as a limit of this example.
coyle-mnist-simulation-method: The Methods state that the experiments are simulations that bypass the quantum state preparation.
coyle-dropout-analogy-limit: The Results state this as a limit of the dropout interpretation.
coyle-evaluation-circuit-cost: Supplementary I states the cost of the evaluation mode.
coyle-expressivity-k1: Follows directly from the definition of the model in Supplementary G.2.
coyle-limits-barren-plateaus: The Results section on drawbacks and limitations states these.
coyle-limit-classical-simulability: The Discussion states this as an open problem.
daskin-power-definition: Section 1 states the definition the later bounds depend on.
daskin-hidden-state-update: Section 2 defines the hidden-state update used in the experiments.
daskin-information-loss-limit: Section 2 states this as a limit of the hidden-state readout.
daskin-sine-setup: Section 4 states the data and training setup.
daskin-complex-data-limit: Section 4 states the trade-off as a limit of the small model used.
